newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE SHARES START WEEK SOFT IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE SHARES START WEEK SOFT IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial shares traded generally soft on Monday in line with market forecasts that they would run soft and quiet ahead of new listings.
"Trade is cautious and soft...and I don't think we can expect much change until the new comers are on stage," one broker said of a couple of new listings expected in the next two months.

These include manufacturing and marketing group Randalls Holdings Ltd which is planning to raise Z$60 million through an offer of 50 million shares, about 24 percent of its total share capital, to investors.
Merspin Ltd, an associate company of Zimbabwe's largest towel manufacturer, Merlin Ltd , is also seeking a listing on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) in April.

On Monday the ZSE's main industrial index fell 34.57 points to 10,443.94 following losses in several key counters, including sugar grower Hippo Valley , which dropped 50 cents to 1,500, and pork company Colcom , which lost 15 cents to 485.
The secondary seven-share mining index slipped 2.20 points to 959.72 in very quiet trade in which nickel miners Bindura traded unchanged at 750.
